newsitem.title: CHINA: Chrysler Corp, China sees $230 mln investment.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler Corp, China sees $230 mln investment.

text.p: Chrysler Corp expects to continue cooperation with China's Beijing Jeep Corp after a 20-year joint venture contract expires in 2004, the China Daily on Friday quoted company officials as saying.

To underline its commitment to ensuring that the joint venture producing the Cherokee jeep, the joint venture Beijing Jeep Corp plans to spend 1.96 billion yuan ($230 million) over the next five years on technical renovation and product development, the newspaper said.
In addition, Beijing Jeep expects that a sleek successor to its ageing, domestically-designed, canvas-topped, military style jeep will hit the roads by 1999 or 2000, the newspaper said.

Beijing Jeep was the only domestic automobile manufacturer that did not cut prices last year as sales slumped, the newspaper said. The firm has no plans to cut the price of its Cherokee jeep this year to ensure the vehicle contains Chrysler's latest technology, it quoted Franc Krebs, president of Beijing Jeep Corp, as saying.

Sales had risen significantly over the last three years, with sales of the Cherokee this year expected to hit 30,000 vehicles, he said. The firm plans to produce 57,000 of its Chinese-designed BJ2020 jeeps this year.

Beijing Jeep sold 71,000 Cherokee and BJ2020 jeeps last year. Beijing Jeep has registered assets of $147 million, with China holding 58 percent and Chrysler 42 percent. That compares with a 62:38 asset breakdown in 1990, the newspaper said.
